# ForgeKernel Kernels

**GPU kernels generated by ForgeKernel on NVIDIA H100 and B200**

**English** | [中文](README_zh.md)

</div>

This directory releases the operator (kernel) code produced by ForgeKernel in the paper
[*ForgeKernel: Self-Evolving Kernels Catching and Surpassing Experts and Agents*](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=EtV3f5BPD4)
(under review at ICLR 2027), plus a kernel ForgeKernel generated after the paper was submitted,
marked "after the paper" below.

ForgeKernel is a self-evolving kernel agent. It reads a reference kernel's architecture from
hardware behavior alone (running, timing and profiling a sealed binary, never its source) and
turns it into an architecture-first curriculum that a coding agent implements. Every accepted
kernel can be sealed and promoted to be the reference of the next run, so optimization continues
past the best known implementation. The paper's kernels are written in
[CuTe DSL](https://docs.nvidia.com/cutlass/media/docs/pythonDSL/overview.html) (`nvidia-cutlass-dsl`);
the post-paper kernel is CUDA C++. None of them was produced with access to the source code of the
library or system it is compared against.

## Layout

Kernels are grouped by operator type, then by operator and GPU:

```
kernels/
├── attention/          dense attention: forward, backward, paged decode/prefill
├── sparse_attention/   DeepSeek sparse attention (DSA) and the DeepSeek-V4.1 fused prefill
├── linear_attention/   Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention
├── gemm/               dense, FP8 and FP8 × FP4 grouped GEMM
└── conv/               2-D and 3-D convolution
```

Each leaf directory holds one kernel (`kernel.py`, plus its CUDA sources for the post-paper
kernel).

## Kernels

Positive numbers mean the ForgeKernel kernel is faster. "Source" is where the number comes from:
paper Figure 3 (against expert libraries), Figure 4 (against other kernel-generation systems),
Table 1 (self-evolution by reference promotion), or after the paper.

### Generations

A Table 1 kernel was produced with the best known kernel sealed as its reference; its speedup is
over that reference, and the number in parentheses is cumulative over the expert library. Where an
operator has several kernels on one GPU, they sit in subdirectories:

- `gen0` is ForgeKernel's first kernel, produced against the expert library (Figure 3).
- `gen1` and `gen2` are successive promotions: each was produced with the previous generation
  sealed as its reference. Attention forward is the only chain the paper promoted twice in
  succession, so it is the only one with `gen1` and `gen2`.
- `from_agent` comes from a single promotion whose reference was written by the /goal agent, not
  by ForgeKernel, so that reference is not part of this directory.

## Environment

| GPU | CUDA | PyTorch | nvidia-cutlass-dsl |
|-|-|-|-|
| H100 SXM (`sm_90a`) | 12.8 or 13.1 | 2.6 or 2.10 | 4.4.2, 4.6.0.dev0 or 4.6.1 |
| B200 (`sm_100a`) | 13.0 | 2.13 | 4.6.0 or 4.6.2 (not used by the CUDA C++ kernel) |

Times are device time (median over
pipelined back-to-back launches); several H100 measurements used SM clocks locked at 1590 MHz.
